picks.game: Boston Red Sox @ New York Yankees
picks.rationale: This AL Wild Card game features a premier pitching matchup between New York's Cam Schlittler, the presumptive AL Cy Young winner with a 1.95 ERA, and Boston's Payton Tolle, who holds a strong 3.03 ERA. Both starters exhibit excellent strikeout capabilities and have historically limited opposing offenses, with the Yankees' projected lineup hitting only 12-for-64 against Tolle and the Red Sox 4-for-32 against Schlittler. The Red Sox pitching staff has a 2.45 ERA over their last 10 games, further supporting a low-scoring affair. With the total line already moving down from 6.5 to 6, sharp money indicates a strong expectation for runs to be at a premium in this playoff contest.

The pitching matchup in this NL Wild Card opener is formidable, with Atlanta's Chris Sale (2.16 ERA) having a dominant 4-0 record and 2.08 ERA against the Phillies this season. Philadelphia counters with Jesús Luzardo (2.86 ERA) as an opener, who, despite a recent shoulder injury, previously threw a 12-strikeout complete game shutout against the Braves. While the Phillies' bullpen has struggled in September with a 5.79 ERA, Sale's ability to go deep into games and Luzardo's potential to limit early runs should keep the score low. The Braves' overall bullpen ERA of 3.44 also provides a solid back end, making the Under a high-confidence play.

Both the White Sox and Astros are employing an opener strategy for this AL Wild Card game, which often leads to more pitching changes and scoring opportunities. Houston's opener, A.J. Blubaugh, has a concerning 7.71 ERA in September with a high home run and elevation rate, making him vulnerable to the White Sox's improving offense. The White Sox have posted a 112 wRC+ and .736 OPS over their last 12 games, while Houston's offense has been red-hot, hitting 25 home runs and slugging .543 in their last 10 games. Both teams' games averaged over 9.2 runs this season, and with high walk rates expected from both openers, the conditions are ripe for an offensive outburst.

The Chicago Cubs boast one of baseball's best offenses in 2026, having scored 55 runs in just six head-to-head matchups against the Padres this season, including a 23-3 victory. Pete Crow-Armstrong has been particularly dominant against San Diego pitching, with 4 home runs and 10 RBIs in those games. Both teams enter this Wild Card series with potent offenses, as both have hit 12 home runs in their last 10 games. While Matthew Boyd (3.91 ERA) starts for the Cubs, the Padres' recent offensive surge, including an 18-6 record in September, suggests they will contribute to a higher-scoring affair.

The Chicago White Sox present significant value as moneyline underdogs in this AL Wild Card matchup, primarily due to their starting pitching advantage. Rookie left-hander Hagen Smith has been exceptional with a 1.29 ERA and 0.96 WHIP, providing a strong foundation for the White Sox. In contrast, Houston is relying on A.J. Blubaugh as an opener, who has struggled recently with a 7.71 ERA in September, indicating vulnerability. While Houston's high-leverage bullpen arms are rested, the White Sox offense has shown recent improvement, with a 112 wRC+ and .736 OPS over their last 12 games, positioning them to capitalize on Houston's bullpen-heavy strategy.
